items.summary: rocThrust single-block thrust::transform_reduce hangs in its result-copy (hipMemcpyWithStream) path on RDNA4 (gfx1201) and the RDNA3.5 APU (gfx1151) when reducing over stdgpu's degenerate capacity-1 full collision-chain table in valid(); gfx90a/gfx1100 unaffected. Worked around in stdgpu PR #484 (transform_reduce_index_device in numeric_detail.h). NEEDS A STANDALONE REPRODUCER before filing upstream: prior attempts (t5 thrust::transform_reduce with bigfunc/lockseq variants, t6 raw-HIP reduction) all PASS; bug only triggers with the genuine unordered_base device object captured by value. RETRY ON THE gfx1201 WINDOWS HOST (RDNA4, RX 9070 XT) -- not reproducible on this gfx90a host. Next attempt: capture the real createDeviceObject(1) unordered_base in its exact post-2-fill state into a minimal reduce functor, stripping stdgpu/rocThrust scaffolding incrementally.

rocThrust unconditionally includes device-compiler builtins (e.g. __builtin_amdgcn_wavefrontsize) in headers reachable from host-side thrust use, so host-only thrust algorithms (thrust::host) cannot compile with a plain CXX compiler as CCCL thrust allows; forces stdgpu HIP-backend consumers to compile affected TUs with the HIP compiler. stotko asked (stdgpu#484 thread) that this limitation be raised with the rocThrust team.
